examples.question: $P(A)=0.5$, $P(B)=0.3$, $P(A\cap B)=0.1$. Find the probability that exactly one of $A,B$ occurs.
$P(A)=0.5$, $P(A\cap B)=0.2$. Find $P(A\cap B')$.
$4$ students are chosen from $6$ boys and $4$ girls. Find the probability that exactly $2$ are girls.
A die has $2$ faces with $1$, $3$ faces with $2$ and $1$ face with $3$. It is rolled once. Find $P(2)$ and $P(1\text{ or }3)$.
